title: RIPR CLI Refusal
description: The minimal document ripr writes to stdout when an argv usage error (unknown command, argument or value; a value flag missing its value; a required flag left out; two flags that cannot be used together; a malformed value) or a context selector miss occurs under an explicit JSON request (#11584, #6834 decision), and, with a reason code and disposition, when a typed `repair`/`continue`/`status` refusal stops before any check under `--json` (#14931), and when an argv-named input (a receipt, a ledger, a cache root) cannot be used (`input_unusable`, #15260). `next` is a help route, a command the refusal's owner composed from typed state (the bound root, the finding listing), or null; it is never lifted from caller-typed values. Exit code (2 for usage errors, 3 for typed refusals) and stderr prose are unchanged. It carries no argv echo and no partial analysis; without a JSON request stdout stays empty.

disposition.description: Present only on a typed repair/continue refusal (#14931): what the caller can do next.

choices.description: Present only on a typed selection refusal (`several_eligible_seams`, `ambiguous_attempts`, #14980): one runnable command per listed seam or attempt, composed from its typed id and the bound root (a seam choice is the command stderr prints; an attempt choice fills that id into the stderr retry line), never lifted from prose. `items` may be fewer than `total` when the listing is bounded.
